m01.q: At what distance is the force between two Lennard-Jones atoms zero?
m01.explain: The force vanishes at the bottom of the potential well, r_min = 2^(1/6) σ ≈ 1.122 σ. At r = σ it is the energy that is zero, not the force.

m01.q: The parameter ε in the Lennard-Jones potential represents
options: the depth of the potential well
m01.explain: ε is the energy needed to separate two atoms from their equilibrium position.

m01.q: The term with a sound theoretical basis (London dispersion) is
m01.explain: The r^-6 term follows from the theory of induced dipoles. The r^-12 term is chosen mainly for computational convenience.

m02.q: Why is velocity Verlet preferred over Euler for MD simulations?
options: It needs fewer force evaluations per step
Its energy oscillates without drifting over long times
m02.explain: Velocity Verlet is symplectic and time reversible, so the total energy does not drift even though it oscillates slightly.

m02.q: If Δt is halved, the energy error of velocity Verlet becomes roughly
m02.explain: The velocity Verlet error scales as Δt², so halving Δt gives about a quarter of the error.

m02.q: The Euler trajectory spirals outwards in phase space. This means
options: the energy of the system grows artificially
m02.explain: An outward spiral shows an oscillation amplitude that keeps growing, i.e. energy added by numerical error.

m03.q: The main purpose of periodic boundary conditions is to
options: remove surface effects in small systems
m03.explain: With an endlessly repeated box no atom sits at a surface, so a small system can represent bulk matter.

m03.q: Why must the cutoff r_c not exceed L/2?
options: So that an atom never interacts with two copies of the same atom
Because of the reduced unit rules
m03.explain: If r_c > L/2, the minimum image convention no longer guarantees that each pair is counted exactly once.

m03.q: A simulation at T* = 1 corresponds to what temperature for an element with ε/k_B = 199 K?
m03.explain: T = T* × ε/k_B, so T* = 1 corresponds to 199 K.

m04.q: In the NVE ensemble, the quantities kept constant are
options: number of particles, volume and temperature
number of particles, volume and total energy
m04.explain: NVE, the microcanonical ensemble, keeps N, V and E fixed. The temperature can fluctuate.

m04.q: What happens if the thermostat coupling time τ_T is increased?
options: The temperature reaches the target faster
The temperature reaches the target more slowly
m04.explain: τ_T is a relaxation time; the larger it is, the weaker the coupling to the heat bath.

m04.q: For a 2D system of N atoms with zero total momentum, the number of degrees of freedom is
m04.explain: Each atom has 2 translational degrees of freedom, minus 2 because the total momentum is set to zero.

m05.q: Why is the probability of speed v = 0 zero in the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution?
options: Only a few velocity directions give a very small speed
m05.explain: The factor v (2D) or v² (3D) reflects the number of velocity directions with the same speed, and it is zero at v = 0.

m05.q: What turns the initial uniform speed distribution into a Maxwell-Boltzmann one?
options: An automatic correction in the program
m05.explain: The simulation runs without a thermostat. Collisions between atoms alone exchange energy and bring the system to equilibrium.

m05.q: The shape of the speed distribution can be used to
options: test whether a simulation has equilibrated
m05.explain: If the speed histogram does not yet match the Maxwell-Boltzmann curve, the system has not reached thermal equilibrium.

m06.q: For an ideal gas, g(r) is
m06.explain: In an ideal gas atomic positions are uncorrelated, so the local density equals the average density.

m06.q: The first shell coordination number of the fcc lattice is
m06.explain: Each atom in an fcc lattice has 12 nearest neighbours at distance a/√2.

m06.q: The feature of g(r) that distinguishes a liquid from a solid is
options: the liquid peaks decay quickly towards 1 after a few shells
m06.explain: A liquid is ordered only locally, so positional correlations vanish after two or three neighbour shells.
